thread:
Maya R: Ran a targeted nsys run on the new flash-attn-fused path + kvcache switch. attaching perfetto link and raw timeline dump.
Maya R: command i used:\n```
nsys profile -o /tmp/attn_sliceprobe --sample=none --trace=nvtx,cuda,cudnn --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --duration=20 --force-overwrite --capture-on-launch true --delay 2 --launch-skip 1 --cuda-mem-usage=true python -m bench.attn_sliceprobe --model ./models/opt-6.7b --seq 2048 --batch 2 --kvcache
```
Maya R: perfetto link: https://perfetto.example.com/redirect/attn-sliceprobe-189050
Maya R: tl;dr: write spikes on kvcache write path when fused-flash kernel selected for long kv writes. CPU->GPU memcpy backlog also visible right before spikes.
Samir: saw the perfetto, nice timeline. those kv write spikes align with flash-fused kernel launches at ~12ms intervals.
Derek: do you have the kernel names/IDs? is it the fused_flash_attn_v2 or flash_attn_fused_unroll?
Maya R: kernels: fused_flash_attn_v2 (sm_89) and flash_attn_fused_unroll_8 (sm_89). nvtx shows both; the hotspot is when fused_flash_attn_v2 returns and we do a large kv write of 1.2MB per token chunk.
PerfBot: [perf alert] kvcache_write_latency > 95p for 200ms window, rule="kvcache_write_spike_v1"
Ashley: are writes synchronous? our path should be async but maybe we're doing a blocking cudaMemcpy for small shards.
Maya R: code snippet from runtime where it writes to cache:\n```
// pseudo
if (kv.size() > KV_WRITE_THRESHOLD) {
  cudaMemcpy(dst, src, size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice); // blocking
  nvtxRangePop();
} else {
  enqueue_async_kv_write(src, dst, size);
}
```
Samir: aha — threshold tuned for old flash kernel. fused_flash grows per-token write size due to larger block packing. threshold too low, so we take blocking path.
Jen L: so kernel selection + batching heuristic are interacting. fused kernel packs bigger KV segments => triggers blocking writes => stalls next kernel launch.
Derek: two quick proposals: 1) increase KV_WRITE_THRESHOLD for sm_89 fused kernels 2) change cudaMemcpy to cudaMemcpyAsync + stream sync only when necessary.
Ashley: +1 on async. but be careful with lifetimes of the temporary buffers. we need to ensure arenas don't get reused before copy completes.
Maya R: I tested increasing threshold from 256KB -> 1.5MB in a dev build and re-ran nsys. write spikes dropped latency 35% for long seqs. but we saw a small burst of GPU memory pressure leading to allocation retries at high concurrency.
Samir: could mitigate with preallocated KV slab for fused path. or fall back to smaller packing at high concurrent sessions.
Jen L: Other observation: when we force the kernel selector to pick the unfused flash (smaller packing), CPU overhead went up slightly but GPU occupancy was better and kvcache writes were steady.
PerfBot: [trace note] nsys stamps: kernel_launches=412, memory_copies=78, kvcache_writes_blocking=24
Derek: action items: Maya to prototype async memcpy + slab pool (PR by EOD). Samir to add heuristic tweak for fused kernels (config flag). Ashley to review buffer lifetime and concurrency model.
Maya R: will do. attaching the trimmed nsys export and perfetto slices in the thread fileshare. also left the raw nvprof counters in /artifacts/189050/.
Ashley: thanks. can you also add a small reproducer script that toggles kernel selector? would help QA.
Maya R: yes i'll add repro under bench/attn_sliceprobe/repro_toggle.sh
Jen L: awesome. let's prioritize this — impacting p90 for seq>=1024 on dedicated pools.
Samir: marking as regression candidate in the release board. cc @oncall
Maya R: thanks all. follow up tomorrow with PRs and updated traces. :thumbsup:
